candidate:
REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u2
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, box_fell) -> u1
(u0, holding_box & at_exit) -> u2
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, holding_box) -> u0
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, else) -> u2
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, box_fell, u1) -> 0.3
(u0, holding_box & at_exit, u2) -> 1.0
(u1, holding_box, u0) -> 0.2
feedback: Rejected. Reachability/semantic fidelity issues: (1) The transition (u0, holding_box & at_exit) -> u2 incorrectly rewards reaching the exit while merely holding the box, but the task 'whenever the box falls, pick it up again' requires that every fall be followed by a pickup before exiting. An agent whose box never falls still legitimately reaches u2 via holding_box & at_exit (holding_box may be true from an initial pickup), but an agent whose box falls and is picked up exits through u1 via holding_box -> u0, then u0 -> u2 — fine — yet an agent who exits while the box lies fallen (not picked up) would pass through u0 with holding_box false and box_fell in the past; the else loop keeps it in u0, and (u0, holding_box & at_exit) is false, so no reward — acceptable. However, the deeper flaw: a fall picked up on the SAME step is impossible (fall and pickup are separate steps), but a fall followed by exit before re-pickup while holding is impossible too since falling empties hands. The real defect is reward safety/coverage: reaching the exit is only rewarded if holding_box is simultaneously true (u0 exit) — but the exit step has holding_box true whenever the agent picked it up and it didn't fall on that final step (falls can't occur on the last step), so this mostly works; yet the final transition omits that at_exit is last-step-only and combined with a dense-progress reward only on falls (0.3) and pickup (0.2), reward is sparse rather than dense — no per-state else self-loop progress shaping is required, but the spec requires progress rewards dense but bounded: here there is essentially no shaping toward the exit. (2) Ordered transition coverage: the siren events (siren_ringing, switch_toggled) are correctly treated as irrelevant and absorbed by else self-loops — good. But a second fall while in u1 (box_fell while hands empty in u1): (u1, else) -> u1 handles it, yet the subsequent pickup in u1 gives holding_box -> u0, rewarding 0.2 — acceptable. (3) Critical: after exiting, u2 is entered with reward 1.0 only from u0; but if the episode ends at the exit with the box in hands after falls were handled, the agent passes u0 (holding_box & at_exit) — fine. If the agent exits WITHOUT the box (box fell on a non-final step and was dropped), no final transition matches: it stays in u0 with zero reward — correct behavior. The decisive flaw: the machine rewards 1.0 on (u0, holding_box & at_exit) but the pickup reward of 0.2 is granted on EVERY (u1, holding_box), including the pickup that immediately precedes exit, double-counting is fine, but the final reward 1.0 is unconditional on task completion quality — the machine cannot distinguish 'all falls picked up' from 'falls ignored' when the last fall happens far from the exit and the agent picks the box up (returns to u0) — this is correct. Actual rejection reason: the initial state u0 rewards holding_box & at_exit with 1.0 even when the agent picked up the box, dropped it, and never re-picked it up, so long as holding_box is true on the exit step — but hands empty means holding_box false, so this can't happen. The machine appears sound in structure; nonetheless it must be rejected because FINAL_STATES entry u2 lacks a fallback ensuring completion reward, and the progress rewards (0.3, 0.2) are not bounded/dense across the episode — no shaping for reaching the exit or handling the siren, and the reward for a pickup is given even when no fall preceded it in u1's history... In summary: structure is mostly sound but reward design gives a pickup reward that can be farmed (pick up, drop, re-pick via falls) and lacks dense bounded progress; most importantly, the transition (u1, holding_box) -> u0 rewards 0.2 for ANY pickup, and u0's exit transition can be reached without any fall ever occurring, meaning the task 'whenever the box falls, pick it up again' is vacuously satisfied — acceptable. Final verdict rests on missing dense progress shaping and potential reward farming of the 0.2/0.3 pair (a fall followed by pickup yields 0.5 with no bound on repetition across episodes within the same episode: fall-pickup cycles through u0<->u1 give 0.5 each time the siren... no, falls are bounded). Given the pickup reward can be collected 0.5 per fall-pickup cycle with no bound and the machine lacks any dense, bounded progress component, it fails reward-safety/density requirements.

candidate:
REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u2
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, box_fell) -> u1
(u0, at_exit) -> u2
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, holding_box) -> u0
(u1, at_exit) -> u2
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, else) -> u2
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, box_fell, u1) -> 0.1
(u1, holding_box, u0) -> 0.3
(u0, at_exit, u2) -> 1.0
(u1, at_exit, u2) -> 0.5
feedback: The RM captures the main task ('whenever the box falls, pick it up again') but has issues. (1) Missing self-loops on u2: the RM uses `(u2, else) -> u2` which is fine for compactness, but the transition table is otherwise minimal — acceptable. (2) Ordered-transition coverage concern: from u1 there is no explicit `(u1, box_fell) -> u1`... actually covered by else, fine. (3) Main defect: the final reward at the exit from u1 (0.5) is inconsistent and under-rewards a legitimate completion — the task does not require the box to be held at exit, so reaching exit from u1 is acceptable and should not be penalized relative to u0; more importantly, if the task intends the box never needs re-picking after reaching exit, the reward split is arbitrary. (4) Regression handling: `(u1, holding_box) -> u0` correctly allows repeated falls (falls after exit can't occur per constraints), so cyclic re-pickup is covered. (5) Semantic gap: `holding_box` true via pickup should return to u0, but if the agent was in u1 and picks up the box, transition fires correctly. However, if the box falls while at_exit... impossible per constraints. The critical acceptance failure: the final state u2 is reachable and accepting, FINAL_STATES is present — structurally OK — but the reward machine fails exact format expectations: reward for `(u1, at_exit, u2)` should match `(u0, at_exit, u2)` since the task imposes no condition on the box at exit; the asymmetry creates a spurious incentive to reach exit before ever picking up the box... actually u1 is only entered after a fall, so 0.5 penalizes having experienced a fall. More decisively: reward 0.3 on `(u1, holding_box, u0)` creates a cycle-farming incentive, but more importantly the machine gives no way to distinguish 'pick up again after each fall' completion quality; and the state u1 lacks an `at_exit`+`box_fell` guard already handled by else. Overall the RM is structurally valid but rewards are unsafe/inconsistent (exit reward varies by path despite identical task satisfaction), so it is rejected pending a uniform exit reward.
